summary: 2 findings checked, both by site-check. 0 confirmed, 0 refuted, 2 unverifiable, 0 not checked. F-001: the cited sites exist and the no-clamp mechanism holds, but the finding's cap value and property name are wrong (max-height min(420px, 100vh - 80px), not a fixed 400px max-block-size); the clipping itself rests on the orchestrator's live Chromium probe, which cannot be repeated here. F-002: the sites and the DOM nesting exist; the one live measurement (Chromium 156) shows no displacement, and the shipped WKWebView engine is unmeasured. No execution method was available: no browser, and no verify-run covers the rendered behaviour.

verifications.evidence: Sites found. (1) research-evidence/verify-F-001-1.txt: keryx ctx rg 'setPosition\(|max-block-size|max-height|innerHeight' over MetaprojectView.tsx, metaproject.css, styles.css, exit 0. MetaprojectView.tsx:181 'setPosition({ left, top: rect.bottom + 4 });' matches. styles.css:143 .menu reads 'position: fixed; z-index: 70; padding: 4px; max-height: min(420px, calc(100vh - 80px)); overflow-y: auto;'. No max-block-size or max-height match in metaproject.css, so .metaproject-filters-pop (metaproject.css:90, display/gap/padding only) adds no clamp. (2) Corrections the site check forces on the finding text: the cap is max-height, not max-block-size, and it is min(420px, 100vh - 80px), so it is viewport-dependent (400px at a 480px window), not a fixed 400px. It still does not depend on the anchor position, so the no-clamp mechanism stands. Not settled here: the clipping itself (popover bottom 531 vs window 480 at 720x480, Details expanded, scrollHeight equals clientHeight 229). That comes from research-evidence/live-filters-popover-720x480.txt, a rendered-screen measurement in Chromium 156 that I cannot repeat and that is not a verify-run. Not checked: light theme, 1180x780 and 1440x900 with the popover open, the native Tauri window.

Sites found. (1) research-evidence/verify-F-002-1.txt: keryx ctx rg 'container:|container-type|position: fixed|createPortal' over apps/desktop/src/metaproject and styles.css, exit 0, 8 matches, completeness reported complete. metaproject.css:9 '.metaproject { container: metaproject / inline-size; }' matches; styles.css:143 .menu is position: fixed. (2) MetaprojectView.tsx:730 opens section className 'flows metaproject' (the container element); the popover div 'menu metaproject-filters-pop' (MetaprojectView.tsx:196) is rendered from '{mode === \'graph\' && filters}' at MetaprojectView.tsx:844, inside that section, so the descendant relationship the finding relies on is real. Placement uses viewport coordinates (MetaprojectView.tsx:178-181). (3) Part of the impact text does not follow from the offset: the Escape and outside-press logic (MetaprojectView.tsx:186-194) use DOM containment (panel.current?.contains, anchor.contains), not coordinates; only the horizontal clamp reads window.innerWidth. (4) research-evidence/live-filters-popover-containing-block.txt (Chromium 156, window 1024x768, read after the pop-in animation): section left 60, top 77; popover rect left 587, top 239, equal to its inline coordinates, so no displacement in that engine. The 720x480 probe (button bottom 225, popover top 232) is the intended 4px gap, i.e. zero offset; the finding's 'consistent with a small offset' reads it the wrong way. Not settled: the shipped desktop app runs in WKWebView (Tauri), and no WebKit measurement exists; whether that engine makes the section the containing block for position: fixed under container-type: inline-size is the open question, and no command here can answer it. Not checked: styles.css:584 (position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 1000 overlay) is a second fixed selector in the verify output; whether it renders inside the section is not established, so the 'only fixed descendant' enumeration is not fully checked.
